name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    # Yama's learn commits touch only the committed memory database, carry
    # [skip ci], and are pushed with the workflow token (which does not trigger
    # workflows). This paths-ignore is the extra guard: [skip ci] is honoured
    # inconsistently across CI systems, and a memory update has nothing to
    # build or test.
    paths-ignore:
      - "reviewer/memory/**"
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        # `engines.node` is >=22, so 20 can no longer install this package.
        # The shape is unchanged: minimum supported, current LTS, latest.
        node-version: [22, 24, 26]

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup PNPM
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@0ebf47130e4866e96fce0953f49152a61190b271 # v6.0.9
        # No `version:` input on purpose. With one, action-setup hard-errors when
        # it disagrees with `packageManager` in package.json; without one it takes
        # the version from that field, so the manifest stays the single source.
        # Do not reintroduce it.

      - name: Setup Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
          cache: "pnpm"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Check formatting
        # Check, never write: `pnpm run format` reformatted the checkout in place
        # and then passed, so CI could never tell a formatted branch from an
        # unformatted one.
        run: pnpm run format:check

      - name: Run linting
        run: |
          echo "🔍 Running ESLint validation with controlled warning limits..."
          pnpm run lint

      - name: 🔒 Security & Environment Validation
        run: |
          echo "🔍 Running build rule enforcement validations..."
          pnpm run validate:all

      - name: Type checking
        run: pnpm run type-check

      - name: Build package
        run: pnpm run build

      - name: Run tests
        # Must stay AFTER the build. The suites are end-to-end by rule: they drive
        # dist/cli/index.js and dist/index.js, never src/. Without dist/ there is
        # nothing to test.
        run: pnpm run test

  build-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup PNPM
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@0ebf47130e4866e96fce0953f49152a61190b271 # v6.0.9

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "26"
          cache: "pnpm"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Check package build
        run: pnpm run prepack

      - name: Verify package contents
        run: |
          pnpm pack
          ls -la dist/

  quality-gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: 🛡️ Code Quality & Security Gate
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Setup PNPM
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@0ebf47130e4866e96fce0953f49152a61190b271 # v6.0.9

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "26"
          cache: "pnpm"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: 🔍 Build Validation
        run: |
          echo "🔍 Running comprehensive build validation..."
          pnpm run validate

      - name: 📝 Commit Message Validation
        # Pass attacker-controllable PR context through env vars, never interpolated
        # into the shell (a branch name or ref can carry shell metacharacters).
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          echo "📝 Validating commit message format..."
          # For PRs, validate the actual PR head commit, not the merge commit
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "pull_request" ]; then
            echo "PR Event: Getting head commit from $HEAD_REF"
            echo "Head SHA: $HEAD_SHA"
            # Use GitHub context to get the commit message directly
            COMMIT_MSG=$(git log -1 --pretty=format:"%s" "$HEAD_SHA")
            echo "Validating PR head commit: $COMMIT_MSG"
          else
            COMMIT_MSG=$(git log -1 --pretty=format:"%s")
            echo "Validating push commit: $COMMIT_MSG"
          fi
          node scripts/commit-validation.cjs "$COMMIT_MSG"

      - name: 🌍 Environment Validation
        run: |
          echo "🌍 Validating environment configuration..."
          pnpm run validate:env

      - name: 🔒 Security Validation
        run: |
          echo "🔒 Running security checks..."
          pnpm run validate:security

      - name: 🛡️ Dependency Audit (production)
        run: |
          echo "🛡️ Auditing production dependencies (advisory)..."
          pnpm audit --prod || true
        continue-on-error: true

      - name: 📊 ESLint Quality Report
        run: |
          echo "📊 Generating ESLint quality report..."
          pnpm run lint --format=stylish
        continue-on-error: true

      - name: 📈 TypeScript Compiler Check
        run: |
          echo "📈 Running TypeScript compiler strict checks on source files..."
          pnpm run type-check

      - name: 🎯 End-to-End Suite (advisory)
        # Was "Code Coverage Analysis". There is no coverage instrument to run:
        # the suites are end-to-end and drive the built artifact, so what this gate
        # can report is whether that artifact behaves — hence the build first.
        # Advisory here; the `test` job is the one that gates.
        run: |
          echo "🎯 Building and running the end-to-end suite..."
          pnpm run build
          pnpm run test || echo "Tests completed with warnings"
        continue-on-error: true

      - name: 📋 Quality Summary
        run: |
          echo "📋 Build Rule Enforcement Summary:"
          echo "✅ Build validation passed"
          echo "✅ Environment validation passed"
          echo "✅ Security validation passed"
          echo "✅ TypeScript compilation passed"
          echo "✅ Commit message format validated"
          echo ""
          echo "🎉 All quality gates passed!"

# .github/workflows/yama.yml — Yama review on every pull request (TASKS:Y6.3).
#
# Two things make this work across runs:
#   fetch-depth: 0     the diff is taken from git, so the base ref has to be there
#   the artifact steps the run store is what makes a re-review incremental; it is a CI
#                      artifact, never a commit
name: yama review

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, closed]

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  review:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # Yama diffs merge-base(base, head)..head with plain git. A shallow clone has no
          # base commit to diff against.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"

      # Carry the previous run's store in, so this review knows what the last one found.
      # First run on a pull request has none; that is a fresh review, not a failure.
      - name: Restore the run store
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          name: yama-store-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          path: .yama/artifacts

      - name: Review
        env:
          GOOGLE_AI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_AI_API_KEY }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          GITHUB_OWNER: ${{ github.repository_owner }}
          GITHUB_REPO: ${{ github.event.repository.name }}
        run: >-
          npx yama review
          --pr ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          --base origin/${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
          --json yama-result.json

      # Always: a run that failed still banked what it did, and that is what you read.
      - name: Keep the run store
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: yama-store-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          path: |
            .yama/artifacts
            yama-result.json
          retention-days: 30

  # Post-merge knowledge update (TASKS:Y7.2). Uncomment once `learn.enabled: true` is set
  # in .yama/yama.yaml. It is a SEPARATE job on a different trigger on purpose: the review
  # path never pays for learning, and this is the only step that needs write access.
  #
  # learn:
  #   if: github.event.pull_request.merged == true
  #   runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  #   permissions:
  #     contents: write        # the ONLY job that needs this
  #     pull-requests: read
  #   steps:
  #     - uses: actions/checkout@v4
  #       with:
  #         # A pull_request checkout is DETACHED. Check the base branch out by name, or
  #         # set learn.branch in .yama/yama.yaml — learn refuses a detached HEAD.
  #         ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
  #     - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
  #       with:
  #         node-version: "22"
  #     - name: Learn
  #       env:
  #         GOOGLE_AI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_AI_API_KEY }}
  #         GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
  #         GITHUB_OWNER: ${{ github.repository_owner }}
  #         GITHUB_REPO: ${{ github.event.repository.name }}
  #       # Run it with --dry-run first and read the plan it prints.
  #       run: npx yama learn --pr ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}

# Exit codes (a CI contract — codes are added, never renumbered):
#   0  the review finished; verdict approve or comment
#   1  the review finished; verdict BLOCK — this step fails the job
#   2  configuration is missing or invalid
#   3  the run itself failed (engine, MCP, platform, or a check)

# Minimal valid mcp.yaml — PLAN.md section 4.
#
# TASKS:Y1.1/Y1.3 — validated by `src/config/schema.ts`; the startup capability
# probe is written against this fixture. Keep the three in step.

# MCP servers to connect at startup. argv arrays, never a shell string.
servers:
  git:
    transport: stdio
    command: npx
    args: ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-git", "--repository", "."]

# capability -> "<server>.<tool>". Absent capability = feature off, never broken.
# Posting capabilities are exposed to the main agent in Delivery only, and never
# to workers (PLAN.md section 3, TASKS:Y5.1) — none are declared here, so this
# fixture exercises the read-only, analysis-only path.
capabilities:
  pr.read: git.git_show
  pr.diff: git.git_diff

# NEGATIVE FIXTURE (TASKS:Y1.1, Y8.1) — a capability id Yama does not know.
# `comment.inline.post` is a plausible typo for `comment.inline.create`, and a
# strict schema is the only thing standing between it and a review that silently
# never posts anything. The error must list the ids that DO exist.
servers:
  forge:
    transport: stdio
    command: node
    args: ["-e", "0"]
capabilities:
  comment.list: forge.list_comments
  comment.inline.post: forge.create_inline

# mini-repo

Fixture consumer repository for Yama's e2e suites (TASKS:Y8.1). Three source files
and a minimal `.yama/` config directory — enough to drive the config loader, the
capability probe and, later, a local-mode review end to end.

Nothing here is real code; the two `src/` files exist so a diff has something to
point at, and `auth.ts` carries the kind of change a rulebook would have opinions
about.

# Synthetic pull request (TASKS:Y8.1)

A pull request that has already been reviewed once, as data — so the recurring-run path
(TASKS:Y7.1) and `yama learn` (TASKS:Y7.2) can be driven end to end with no forge, no MCP
server and no credentials anywhere.

| File | What it stands in for |
|---|---|
| `comments.json` | exactly what a `comment.list` tool returns: two forges' shapes in one list, three of the comments carrying Yama's `<!-- yama:finding:… -->` markers, one written by a human replying to one of them |
| `prior-run.json` | the run report the previous review banked — its `headSha` is the left-hand side of the incremental diff |
| `prior-findings.json` | the findings ledger that review left behind: what a re-review has to account for |

The two shapes in `comments.json` are deliberate. A GitHub-style comment puts the text in
`body` and the id in `id`; a Bitbucket-style one nests it under `content.raw`. Product code
never learns which is which — `readComments` reads both — and a fixture that only carried
one of them would let a forge-specific reader pass.

name: GitHub Copilot PR Review

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

jobs:
  copilot-review:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: 🤖 GitHub Copilot PR Review

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Setup PNPM
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@0ebf47130e4866e96fce0953f49152a61190b271 # v6.0.9
        # Version comes from `packageManager` in package.json; a `version:` input
        # here only creates a second place for it to disagree, and action-setup
        # hard-errors on that disagreement.

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "26"
          cache: "pnpm"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install

      # NOTE: The AI code-review step previously used `coderabbitai/openai-pr-reviewer`,
      # which was removed upstream and no longer resolves on GitHub Actions
      # (causing this job to fail on every PR). AI review is now handled by the
      # dedicated `Yama review` workflow (yama-review.yml). The remaining steps
      # here keep build-rule validation + the status comment.

      - name: 🔍 Validate PR Against Build Rules
        run: |
          echo "🔍 Running build rule validation on PR changes..."

          # Run all validations to ensure PR compliance
          pnpm run validate:all || echo "⚠️ Build rule validation completed with warnings"

          # Check commit message format for PR
          echo "📝 Validating PR commit messages..."
          git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD | while read commit; do
            commit_msg=$(echo "$commit" | cut -d' ' -f2-)
            echo "Checking: $commit_msg"
            node scripts/commit-validation.cjs "$commit_msg" || echo "⚠️ Commit message needs attention"
          done

      - name: Check Comment Permissions
        id: check-permissions
        run: |
          # Check if this is an external contributor PR using repository IDs for security
          if [ "${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.id }}" != "${{ github.event.repository.id }}" ]; then
            echo "🔒 External contributor PR detected - comment posting will be skipped due to GitHub security restrictions"
            echo "can_comment=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          else
            echo "🏠 Internal contributor PR - comment posting enabled"
            echo "can_comment=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi

      - name: Find existing AI review comment
        if: steps.check-permissions.outputs.can_comment == 'true'
        uses: peter-evans/find-comment@3eae4d37986fb5a8592848f6a574fdf654e61f9e # v3.1.0
        id: find-ai-comment
        with:
          issue-number: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          comment-author: "github-actions[bot]"
          body-includes: AI-Powered PR Analysis

      - name: 📊 Consolidated PR Analysis & Compliance Summary
        if: steps.check-permissions.outputs.can_comment == 'true'
        uses: peter-evans/create-or-update-comment@71345be0265236311c031f5c7866368bd1eff043 # v4.0.0
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          issue-number: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          comment-id: ${{ steps.find-ai-comment.outputs.comment-id }}
          edit-mode: replace
          body: |
            ## 🤖 AI Review & Build Compliance ✅

            **Status**: AI analysis complete • Build rules validated • Ready for review

            <details>
            <summary>📊 View detailed analysis results</summary>

            ### 🛡️ Analysis Complete
            - ✅ Security scan (vulnerabilities, API keys)
            - ✅ TypeScript safety & code quality
            - ✅ Error handling & best practices
            - ✅ Build rule enforcement validated
            - ✅ Commit format & compliance checks

            ### 📋 Ready for Merge When
            - [ ] All CI checks passing
            - [ ] Manual review approved
            - [ ] Any AI-flagged issues resolved

            </details>

            ---
            *🤖 AI analysis complete - check individual code comments for specific feedback*

name: Release and Publish

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

permissions:
  contents: write
  packages: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write
  id-token: write # Required for npm provenance

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup PNPM
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@0ebf47130e4866e96fce0953f49152a61190b271 # v6.0.9
        # Version comes from `packageManager` in package.json; a `version:` input
        # here only creates a second place for it to disagree, and action-setup
        # hard-errors on that disagreement.

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "24"
          cache: "pnpm"
          registry-url: https://registry.npmjs.org/

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install

      - name: Build package
        run: pnpm run build

      - name: Run tests
        # After the build, not before it: the suites are end-to-end and drive
        # dist/cli/index.js and dist/index.js, so there is nothing to test until
        # the package is built.
        run: pnpm run test

  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      packages: write
      issues: write
      pull-requests: write
      id-token: write # Required for OIDC authentication with npm provenance
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Setup PNPM
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@0ebf47130e4866e96fce0953f49152a61190b271 # v6.0.9
        # Version comes from `packageManager` in package.json.

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "24"
          registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org"
          cache: "pnpm"

      - name: Upgrade npm for OIDC support
        run: npm install -g npm@latest

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install

      - name: Build package
        run: pnpm run build

      - name: Release with semantic-release
        run: npx semantic-release
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          HUSKY: "0" # Disable git hooks during automated release commits

      - name: Setup Node for GitHub Packages
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "24"
          registry-url: "https://npm.pkg.github.com"
          scope: "@juspay"

      - name: Publish to GitHub Packages
        run: |
          VERSION=$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")
          if npm view "@juspay/yama@${VERSION}" version --registry https://npm.pkg.github.com >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "ℹ️ @juspay/yama@${VERSION} already on GitHub Packages — skipping."
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "📦 Publishing @juspay/yama@${VERSION} to GitHub Packages..."
          # git-checks must come from config, not argv: pnpm forwards unknown CLI
          # flags to npm, and npm errors on --git-checks (EUNKNOWNCONFIG).
          pnpm config set git-checks false
          pnpm publish --access public --registry https://npm.pkg.github.com
          echo "✅ Published to GitHub Packages successfully!"
        env:
          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

name: Yama learn

# The merge event is the ONLY trigger that reliably identifies which pull
# request merged. This repository rebases, so commits carry no pull request
# number and a `push` trigger would attribute feedback to the wrong pull
# request — or to none.
#
# There is deliberately no paths-ignore here. The loop guards for this workflow
# are the bot-author refusal below, `[skip ci]` on the commit learn makes, and
# the workflow GITHUB_TOKEN it pushes with (pushes made with that token do not
# trigger workflows). The paths-ignore that matters lives on CI's push trigger,
# where a learn commit DOES land.
on:
  # Chained AFTER the release workflow on the default branch: the release run
  # has finished (its version commit pushed and all) before learn is even
  # queued, so learn's push cannot race the release bot's. `pull_request:
  # closed` or a plain `push` would both re-open that race — learn spends
  # minutes on the retrospective and refuses to force-push into a branch that
  # moved underneath it.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["Release and Publish"]
    types: [completed]

  # Recovery lever: a learn that failed for an environmental reason can be
  # re-run for the same pull request. The merged-and-human guard is re-checked
  # below from GitHub's own record, so a dispatch cannot aim the write job at
  # an unmerged or bot-authored pull request.
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      pr:
        description: "Merged pull request number to learn from"
        required: true
        type: string

# Serialised: two learn runs would race each other pushing to main, and the
# loser would be rebased onto a memory it never read.
concurrency:
  group: yama-learn
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  learn:
    # Only a MERGED pull request teaches anything. A closed-unmerged one was
    # rejected, and learning from it would record conventions nobody adopted.
    if: >
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
      github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30

    steps:
      - name: Resolve the pull request this run learns from
        id: target
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
          DISPATCH_PR: ${{ inputs.pr }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -n "${DISPATCH_PR:-}" ]; then
            PR="$DISPATCH_PR"
          else
            # Which pull request produced this commit. Works for squash, merge
            # and rebase merges alike: GitHub associates the resulting commit
            # with the pull request it came from.
            PR=$(gh api "repos/${REPOSITORY}/commits/${HEAD_SHA}/pulls" \
                   --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null)] | sort_by(.merged_at) | reverse | .[0].number // empty')
          fi
          if [ -z "${PR:-}" ]; then
            echo "::notice::No merged pull request behind ${HEAD_SHA} — a direct push has no discussion to learn from."
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi
          # The guard the closed trigger used to carry, re-checked from the
          # platform's own record so every trigger path is held to it.
          merged=$(gh api "repos/${REPOSITORY}/pulls/${PR}" --jq '.merged')
          author=$(gh api "repos/${REPOSITORY}/pulls/${PR}" --jq '.user.login')
          [ "$merged" = "true" ] || { echo "::error::PR #${PR} is not merged"; exit 1; }
          [ "$author" != "github-actions[bot]" ] || { echo "::error::PR #${PR} is bot-authored — refusing the self-feed loop"; exit 1; }
          echo "Learning from PR #${PR} (merged, authored by ${author})."
          echo "pr=${PR}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Checkout
        if: steps.target.outputs.run == 'true'
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Named, not detached: learn refuses to commit on a detached HEAD,
          # and a pull_request checkout is detached by default.
          ref: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
          # The WORKFLOW token is the push credential: this job declares
          # `contents: write`, and the learn commit's [skip ci] plus CI's
          # paths-ignore break the loop. YAMA_GITHUB_TOKEN is the API/MCP read
          # credential only — it has no push access to this repository, and the
          # first production learn died pushing with it (403).
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Setup PNPM
        if: steps.target.outputs.run == 'true'
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@0ebf47130e4866e96fce0953f49152a61190b271 # v6.0.9
        # Version comes from `packageManager` in package.json; passing one here
        # only creates a second place for it to disagree.

      - name: Setup Node.js
        if: steps.target.outputs.run == 'true'
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: "pnpm"
          cache-dependency-path: reviewer/pnpm-lock.yaml

      - name: Install the reviewer
        if: steps.target.outputs.run == 'true'
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --dir reviewer

      - name: Set the commit identity
        if: steps.target.outputs.run == 'true'
        # learn.mjs shells out to plain `git commit`; it never passes an author
        # of its own, on purpose — the identity a repository's agent commits
        # under is the repository's decision, not the tool's. A runner has no
        # git identity configured, so without this the commit fails at the very
        # end, after the whole retrospective has been paid for.
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

      - name: Learn
        if: steps.target.outputs.run == 'true'
        # One agent turn reads the merged pull request through the github MCP
        # server (config.learnPrompt) and distills its learnings into
        # memory/hippocampus.sqlite; then learn.mjs checkpoints the WAL, stages
        # exactly that file, reads the staged set back out of git, and commits
        # and pushes with [skip ci] — never a force push. A refused or failed
        # write exits non-zero, so a silent no-op cannot pass for a successful
        # learn.
        env:
          YAMA_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.YAMA_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          LITELLM_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.LITELLM_API_KEY }}
          LITELLM_BASE_URL: ${{ secrets.LITELLM_BASE_URL }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ steps.target.outputs.pr }}
        working-directory: reviewer
        run: |
          node index.mjs learn "pr=$PR_NUMBER" 2>&1 | tee learn-run.log
          exit "${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

      - name: Archive the run log
        # A run that failed still logged what it did, and that is what you read.
        if: always()
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: yama-learn-${{ steps.target.outputs.pr || 'none' }}-${{ github.run_id }}
          path: reviewer/learn-run.log
          retention-days: 14

name: Single Commit Per Branch Enforcement

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main, develop]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

jobs:
  enforce-single-commit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: 🔒 Single Commit Policy Validation

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Validate Single Commit Policy
        id: validate
        # Route all GitHub context through env vars — branch names (HEAD_REF/
        # BASE_REF/REF_NAME) are attacker-controllable and must never be
        # interpolated directly into the shell.
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.head_ref }}
          REF_NAME: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          HEAD_REPO_ID: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.id }}
          BASE_REPO_ID: ${{ github.event.repository.id }}
        run: |
          # Determine the base branch and current branch
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "pull_request" ]; then
            BASE_BRANCH="origin/$BASE_REF"
            BRANCH_NAME="$HEAD_REF"

            # Handle external vs internal contributors differently using repository IDs for security
            if [ "$HEAD_REPO_ID" != "$BASE_REPO_ID" ]; then
              # External contributor - use the PR head SHA directly
              CURRENT_BRANCH="HEAD"
              echo "📡 External contributor detected"
              echo "🔍 Head repository ID: $HEAD_REPO_ID"
              echo "🔍 Base repository ID: $BASE_REPO_ID"
              echo "🔍 Using PR head SHA: $HEAD_SHA"

              # For external PRs, checkout the actual PR commit (not the merge commit)
              echo "🔄 Checking out PR head commit for validation..."
              git checkout "$HEAD_SHA"
              CURRENT_BRANCH="HEAD"
            else
              # Internal branch - can checkout the actual branch
              echo "🏠 Internal contributor detected"
              echo "🔄 Switching to actual PR head branch for validation..."
              git checkout "origin/$HEAD_REF"
              CURRENT_BRANCH="origin/$HEAD_REF"
            fi
          else
            BASE_BRANCH="origin/main"
            CURRENT_BRANCH="HEAD"
            BRANCH_NAME="$REF_NAME"
          fi

          echo "🔍 Validating single commit policy..."
          echo "Base branch: $BASE_BRANCH"
          echo "Current branch: $BRANCH_NAME"

          # Ensure we have the latest refs
          git fetch origin

          # Count commits ahead of base branch
          COMMIT_COUNT=$(git rev-list --count $CURRENT_BRANCH ^$BASE_BRANCH 2>/dev/null || echo "0")

          echo "commits_ahead=$COMMIT_COUNT" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "branch_name=$BRANCH_NAME" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "base_branch=$BASE_BRANCH" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          echo "📊 Commits ahead of base: $COMMIT_COUNT"

          # Validate commit count
          if [ $COMMIT_COUNT -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "✅ Branch is up to date with base branch"
            echo "status=up_to_date" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          elif [ $COMMIT_COUNT -eq 1 ]; then
            echo "✅ Branch contains exactly 1 commit - POLICY COMPLIANT"
            echo "status=compliant" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            
            # Get the single commit details
            COMMIT_HASH=$(git rev-list -1 $CURRENT_BRANCH ^$BASE_BRANCH)
            COMMIT_MSG=$(git log -1 --pretty=format:"%s" $COMMIT_HASH)
            COMMIT_AUTHOR=$(git log -1 --pretty=format:"%an" $COMMIT_HASH)
            
            echo "📝 Commit: $COMMIT_MSG"
            echo "👤 Author: $COMMIT_AUTHOR"
            echo "🔑 Hash: $COMMIT_HASH"
            
            echo "commit_message=$COMMIT_MSG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "commit_hash=$COMMIT_HASH" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "commit_author=$COMMIT_AUTHOR" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            
          else
            echo "❌ POLICY VIOLATION: Branch contains $COMMIT_COUNT commits"
            echo "status=violation" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            
            # Get details of all commits for the error message
            echo "📋 Commits in this branch:"
            git log --oneline $CURRENT_BRANCH ^$BASE_BRANCH
          fi

      - name: Validate Commit Message Format
        if: steps.validate.outputs.status == 'compliant'
        # The commit message is fully attacker-controlled; pass it via env, never
        # interpolate a step output into the shell.
        env:
          COMMIT_MSG: ${{ steps.validate.outputs.commit_message }}
        run: |
          echo "🔍 Validating commit message format: '$COMMIT_MSG'"

          # Check semantic commit format: type(scope)!: description
          #
          # The `!` is the Conventional Commits breaking-change marker. It was
          # missing here while scripts/commit-validation.cjs (the local hook)
          # accepted it and semantic-release reads it to cut a major — so a
          # correctly-formatted breaking commit passed the hook and failed CI.
          if ! echo "$COMMIT_MSG" | grep -qE "^[a-z]+(\([^)]+\))?!?: .+"; then
            echo "❌ Commit message doesn't follow semantic format"
            echo "Expected: type(scope): description"
            echo "Received: $COMMIT_MSG"
            echo ""
            echo "Valid examples:"
            echo "  feat(auth): add OAuth2 authentication flow"
            echo "  feat(api)!: drop the v1 endpoints (breaking)"
            echo "  fix(api): resolve null pointer exception in user service"
            echo "  docs(readme): update installation instructions"
            exit 1
          fi

          echo "✅ Commit message format is valid"

      - name: Check for Merge Commits
        if: steps.validate.outputs.status == 'compliant'
        env:
          BASE_BRANCH: ${{ steps.validate.outputs.base_branch }}
        run: |

          # Check for merge commits in the branch
          MERGE_COMMITS=$(git rev-list --merges HEAD ^$BASE_BRANCH)
          if [ -n "$MERGE_COMMITS" ]; then
            echo "❌ POLICY VIOLATION: Branch contains merge commits"
            echo "Merge commits are not allowed in feature branches."
            echo "Please rebase your branch instead of merging."
            echo ""
            echo "To fix:"
            echo "  git rebase $BASE_BRANCH"
            echo "  git push --force-with-lease"
            exit 1
          fi

          echo "✅ No merge commits found"

      - name: Provide Squash Instructions
        if: steps.validate.outputs.status == 'violation'
        env:
          COMMIT_COUNT: ${{ steps.validate.outputs.commits_ahead }}
          BRANCH_NAME: ${{ steps.validate.outputs.branch_name }}
        run: |
          echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
          echo "🚫 SINGLE COMMIT POLICY VIOLATION"
          echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
          echo ""
          echo "❌ Branch '$BRANCH_NAME' contains $COMMIT_COUNT commits"
          echo "✅ Yama requires exactly 1 commit per branch"
          echo ""
          echo "🔧 TO FIX - Squash your commits:"
          echo ""
          echo "1. Interactive rebase to squash commits:"
          echo "   git rebase -i HEAD~$COMMIT_COUNT"
          echo ""
          echo "2. In the editor, change 'pick' to 'squash' (or 's') for all commits except the first"
          echo "3. Save and close the editor"
          echo "4. Edit the commit message in the next editor"
          echo "5. Force push the squashed commit:"
          echo "   git push --force-with-lease"
          echo ""
          echo "🎯 Alternative - Reset and recommit:"
          echo "   git reset --soft HEAD~$COMMIT_COUNT"
          echo "   git commit -m 'type(scope): your combined commit message'"
          echo "   git push --force-with-lease"
          echo ""
          echo "📋 Current commits that need squashing:"
          git log --oneline HEAD~$COMMIT_COUNT..HEAD
          echo ""
          echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"

          exit 1

      - name: Check Comment Permissions
        if: steps.validate.outputs.status == 'compliant'
        id: check-permissions
        run: |
          # Check if this is an external contributor PR using repository IDs for security
          if [ "${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.id }}" != "${{ github.event.repository.id }}" ]; then
            echo "🔒 External contributor PR detected - comment posting will be skipped due to GitHub security restrictions"
            echo "can_comment=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          else
            echo "🏠 Internal contributor PR - comment posting enabled"
            echo "can_comment=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi

      - name: Find existing comment
        if: steps.validate.outputs.status == 'compliant' && steps.check-permissions.outputs.can_comment == 'true'
        uses: peter-evans/find-comment@3eae4d37986fb5a8592848f6a574fdf654e61f9e # v3.1.0
        id: find-comment
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          issue-number: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          comment-author: "github-actions[bot]"
          body-includes: Single Commit Policy

      - name: Post Minimal Success Comment
        if: steps.validate.outputs.status == 'compliant' && steps.check-permissions.outputs.can_comment == 'true'
        uses: peter-evans/create-or-update-comment@71345be0265236311c031f5c7866368bd1eff043 # v4.0.0
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          issue-number: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          comment-id: ${{ steps.find-comment.outputs.comment-id }}
          body: |
            ## ✅ Single Commit Policy - COMPLIANT

            **Status**: Policy requirements met • 1 commit • Valid format • Ready for merge

            <details>
            <summary>📊 View validation details</summary>

            ### 📝 Commit Details
            - **Hash**: `${{ steps.validate.outputs.commit_hash }}`
            - **Message**: ${{ steps.validate.outputs.commit_message }}
            - **Author**: ${{ steps.validate.outputs.commit_author }}

            ### ✅ Validation Results
            - Single commit requirement met
            - No merge commits in branch
            - Semantic commit message format verified
            - Ready for squash merge to main branch

            </details>

            ---
            *🤖 Automated validation by Yama Single Commit Enforcement*
          edit-mode: replace

      - name: Generate Policy Summary
        if: always()
        run: |
          echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
          echo "🔒 YAMA SINGLE COMMIT POLICY ENFORCEMENT SUMMARY"
          echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"

          STATUS="${{ steps.validate.outputs.status }}"
          case $STATUS in
            "compliant")
              echo "✅ STATUS: POLICY COMPLIANT"
              echo "✅ Single commit requirement satisfied"
              echo "✅ Ready for merge to main branch"
              ;;
            "violation")
              echo "❌ STATUS: POLICY VIOLATION" 
              echo "❌ Multiple commits detected"

              ;;
            "up_to_date")
              echo "ℹ️  STATUS: BRANCH UP TO DATE"
              echo "ℹ️  No new commits to validate"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "⚠️  STATUS: UNKNOWN"
              ;;
          esac

          echo ""
          echo "📋 Policy Requirements:"
          echo "  • Exactly 1 commit per branch"
          echo "  • Semantic commit message format: type(scope): description" 
          echo "  • No merge commits allowed"
          echo "  • Squash merge enforced at branch protection level"
          echo ""
          echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"

name: Yama review

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]

# One review per pull request at a time. A second push while a review is running
# would race the first on comment markers and could duplicate comments.
concurrency:
  group: yama-review-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  review:
    # Drafts are not ready to be reviewed, and Yama must never review its own
    # learning commits.
    if: >
      github.event.pull_request.draft == false &&
      github.event.pull_request.user.login != 'github-actions[bot]'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Comfortably above the reviewer's per-prompt turn budget
    # (reviewer/config.json timeouts), so a slow model is cut off by the agent —
    # which reports honestly — rather than by the runner, which kills the job
    # and reports nothing.
    timeout-minutes: 90

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The reviewer reads code from disk; full history keeps base/head
          # diffs correct for the graph server and git-based inspection.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Setup PNPM
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@0ebf47130e4866e96fce0953f49152a61190b271 # v6.0.9
        # Version comes from `packageManager` in package.json; passing one here
        # only creates a second place for it to disagree.

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: "pnpm"
          cache-dependency-path: reviewer/pnpm-lock.yaml

      - name: Setup uv (code-review-graph server)
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@20cfd1bf945f4377ade1205e4dbc17946fc9a30d # v10.0.1

      - name: Build the code-review-graph index
        # Builds (or updates) the graph store at the repo root, which also
        # warms uvx's package cache. The reviewer's graph tools answer from
        # this index — an unbuilt graph is why they return nothing. Failure
        # is non-fatal: the review runs without graph context.
        run: uvx --from code-review-graph==2.3.7 code-review-graph build || echo "graph build failed — the review runs without it"

      - name: Install the reviewer
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --dir reviewer

      - name: Review
        # The prompts-driven reviewer (reviewer/): runs reviewer/prompts.json
        # top to bottom in one session — review and post comments, then
        # validate what landed. A failed prompt aborts the run and fails this
        # job.
        env:
          YAMA_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.YAMA_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          LITELLM_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.LITELLM_API_KEY }}
          LITELLM_BASE_URL: ${{ secrets.LITELLM_BASE_URL }}
          # Branch names are attacker-controllable; they go through env, never
          # straight into the shell.
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
        working-directory: reviewer
        run: |
          node index.mjs run "pr=$PR_NUMBER" "branch=$HEAD_REF" 2>&1 | tee review-run.log
          exit "${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

      - name: Archive the run log
        # A run that failed still logged what it did, and that is what you read.
        if: always()
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: yama-review-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}-${{ github.run_id }}
          path: reviewer/review-run.log
          retention-days: 14

name: "Yama review"
description: "Prompts-driven pull request review that reads the checked-out repository's Yama config and posts what it finds."

# Two things this action depends on, both deliberate:
#
#  1. The repository must already be checked out (actions/checkout@v4,
#     fetch-depth: 0) — the reviewer and the code graph read code from disk.
#  2. The checkout root must carry the reviewer's config files: config.json,
#     MCP.json, prompts.json and skills/. `npx yama init` scaffolds them.
#
# Model-provider credentials are NOT inputs here. The reviewer reads whichever
# env vars the repository's config.json provider needs (LITELLM_API_KEY,
# OPENAI_API_KEY, …) — set them as `env:` on the step that uses this action;
# composite steps inherit the caller's env.

inputs:
  pr:
    description: "Pull request number. Defaults to the triggering pull request."
    required: false
  branch:
    description: "Branch under review. Defaults to the triggering pull request's head ref."
    required: false
  yama-version:
    description: >
      npm version range to install. Pinned to the major this action's inputs and
      config shape belong to: installing "latest" would silently run a different
      major against a v6 config layout, which fails in ways that look like a
      broken review rather than a version mismatch.
    required: false
    default: "^6.0.0"
  vcs-token:
    description: >
      Token for the GitHub MCP server, forwarded to the run as both
      YAMA_GITHUB_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN so either name works in MCP.json. Pass
      it through a NON-reserved env name in the calling workflow — the reserved
      GitHub token is not reliably forwarded into a composite action.

      Never write that value with GitHub-Actions expression braces anywhere in
      this manifest: the runner evaluates such expressions even inside
      description strings, the secrets context does not exist at manifest load,
      and the whole action then fails to load with "Unrecognized named-value:
      secrets". scripts/build-validations.cjs fails the build if one appears
      here.
    required: false
  node-version:
    description: "Node version. Yama requires 22 or newer."
    required: false
    default: "22"

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Verify the checkout
      shell: bash
      working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        if [ ! -d .git ]; then
          echo "::error::Yama needs the repository checked out. Add actions/checkout@v4 with fetch-depth: 0 before this step."
          exit 1
        fi
        if [ ! -f config.json ] || [ ! -f prompts.json ]; then
          echo "::error::No Yama config in the checkout root. Run \`npx yama init\`, fill config.json, and commit the result."
          exit 1
        fi

    - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version: ${{ inputs.node-version }}

    - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10

    - name: Build the code-review-graph index
      # Builds (or updates) the graph store at the checkout root, which also
      # warms uvx's package cache. The reviewer's graph tools answer from this
      # index. Failure is non-fatal: the review runs without graph context.
      shell: bash
      working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
      run: uvx --from code-review-graph==2.3.7 code-review-graph build || echo "graph build failed — the review runs without it"

    - name: Review
      # Runs the repository's prompts.json top to bottom in one session. A
      # failed prompt aborts the run and fails this step — an aborted review
      # must never read as a clean one.
      shell: bash
      working-directory: ${{ github.workspace }}
      env:
        # Inputs reach the shell ONLY through environment variables, never by
        # template interpolation into this script: `inputs.branch` is routinely
        # wired to `github.head_ref`, which a fork controls.
        GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.vcs-token }}
        YAMA_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.vcs-token }}
        YAMA_INPUT_PR: ${{ inputs.pr || github.event.pull_request.number }}
        YAMA_INPUT_BRANCH: ${{ inputs.branch || github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
        YAMA_INPUT_VERSION: ${{ inputs.yama-version }}
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        ARGS=(run)
        if [ -n "${YAMA_INPUT_PR:-}" ]; then ARGS+=("pr=$YAMA_INPUT_PR"); fi
        if [ -n "${YAMA_INPUT_BRANCH:-}" ]; then ARGS+=("branch=$YAMA_INPUT_BRANCH"); fi
        npx --yes "@juspay/yama@$YAMA_INPUT_VERSION" "${ARGS[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "${RUNNER_TEMP}/yama-review.log"
        exit "${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

    - name: Archive the run log
      # A run that failed still logged what it did, and that is what you read.
      if: always()
      continue-on-error: true
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: yama-review-${{ inputs.pr || github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_id }}
        path: ${{ runner.temp }}/yama-review.log
        retention-days: 14

# .yama/mcp.yaml — MCP servers, and the capability map (Bitbucket).
#
# The same capability ids as every other forge; only the right-hand side changes. That is
# the contract: Yama's code knows capabilities, this file knows tool names.
#
# Two forms are accepted:
#
#   <capability>: <server>.<tool>
#
#   <capability>:
#     tool: <server>.<tool>
#     args: { workspace: "${BITBUCKET_WORKSPACE}", pull_request_id: "${pr}" }
#
# `${pr}` / `${branch}` / `${base}` / `${mode}` come from the run target; everything else
# is an environment variable, expanded at load time and loud when unset.
#
# TOOL NAMES DIFFER BETWEEN MCP SERVER VERSIONS. Run `yama doctor` after `yama init`: it
# connects each server, prints exactly which tools it exposes, and marks any capability
# pointing at a name that is not there as BROKEN. Fix those rows here and re-run it.
#
# Note what is NOT here: nothing maps the diff. Yama takes it from git
# (merge-base(base, head)..head), which is deterministic, costs no API call, and reads the
# same on every forge — the platform is only ever asked for comments and the verdict.

version: 1

servers:
  bitbucket:
    transport: stdio
    command: npx
    args: ["-y", "@nexus2520/bitbucket-mcp-server"]
    env:
      BITBUCKET_USERNAME: "${BITBUCKET_USERNAME}"
      BITBUCKET_APP_PASSWORD: "${BITBUCKET_APP_PASSWORD}"

capabilities:
  # --- review phase
  pr.read:
    tool: bitbucket.get_pull_request
    args:
      workspace: "${BITBUCKET_WORKSPACE}"
      repository: "${BITBUCKET_REPO}"
      pull_request_id: "${pr}"
  # pr.diff is deliberately unmapped — see the note above.
  comment.list:
    tool: bitbucket.get_pull_request_comments
    args:
      workspace: "${BITBUCKET_WORKSPACE}"
      repository: "${BITBUCKET_REPO}"
      pull_request_id: "${pr}"

  # --- delivery phase
  comment.inline.create:
    tool: bitbucket.add_comment
    args:
      workspace: "${BITBUCKET_WORKSPACE}"
      repository: "${BITBUCKET_REPO}"
      pull_request_id: "${pr}"
  # Answering a comment already on the pull request (the recurring-run case). On this
  # server it is the SAME tool as an inline comment — a reply is one that carries the id
  # of the comment it answers, which the agent supplies along with the text.
  comment.reply:
    tool: bitbucket.add_comment
    args:
      workspace: "${BITBUCKET_WORKSPACE}"
      repository: "${BITBUCKET_REPO}"
      pull_request_id: "${pr}"
  comment.summary.create:
    tool: bitbucket.add_comment
    args:
      workspace: "${BITBUCKET_WORKSPACE}"
      repository: "${BITBUCKET_REPO}"
      pull_request_id: "${pr}"
  # verdict.set:
  #   tool: bitbucket.approve_pull_request
  #   args: { workspace: "${BITBUCKET_WORKSPACE}", repository: "${BITBUCKET_REPO}", pull_request_id: "${pr}" }

# Connections, and the capability map — how Yama reviews Yama's own pull requests.
#
# THE CAPABILITY MAP IS THE WHOLE POINT. Yama's code never spells a platform tool name: it
# asks for a CAPABILITY and this file says which tool provides it, with the arguments every
# call of that tool needs. Moving to another forge is an edit here, not a code change.
#
# Two forms are accepted:
#
#   <capability>: <server>.<tool>
#
#   <capability>:
#     tool: <server>.<tool>
#     args: { owner: "…", pullNumber: "${pr}" }
#
# In `args`, `${pr}` / `${branch}` / `${base}` / `${mode}` come from the run target and
# everything else is an environment variable, expanded at load time and loud when unset.
# An unmapped capability is switched OFF, never broken.
#
# Note what is NOT here: nothing maps the diff. Yama takes it from git
# (merge-base(base, head)..head) — deterministic, no API call, and identical on every
# forge. The platform is only ever asked for the pull request, its comments, and posting.

version: 1

servers:
  github:
    # GitHub's HOSTED MCP server. No process to install, no npx download on every CI run,
    # and it tracks GitHub's own API without a version bump here.
    transport: http
    url: https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/
    headers:
      # A non-reserved variable name on purpose: ${GITHUB_TOKEN} is not reliably forwarded
      # into a composite action, so the workflow passes the token as YAMA_GITHUB_TOKEN.
      # Server variables are expanded at CONNECT time, not at load time — a local review
      # that never talks to GitHub does not need this set.
      Authorization: "Bearer ${YAMA_GITHUB_TOKEN}"
    # A hang detector, not a budget.
    timeoutMs: 30000

  # Tree-sitter code graph (github.com/tirth8205/code-review-graph): out-of-diff context
  # for the reviewer — blast radius, callers and dependents, flows, architecture overview.
  # The workflow warms the uvx cache so connect stays inside its timeout; a machine
  # without uvx, or a failed spawn, is a named degradation, never a failed review.
  # Workers share the host's MCP connections on NeuroLink 12.2, so ONE process serves
  # the whole run (the v4 per-worker respawn deadlocked on uv's cache lock).
  code-review-graph:
    transport: stdio
    command: uvx
    args: ["--from", "code-review-graph==2.3.7", "code-review-graph", "serve"]
    timeoutMs: 60000
    # Read/analyze only — exposed to the REVIEW stages, never delivery. Mutating or
    # expensive tools (refactor, embeddings, wiki, cross-repo) stay unexposed.
    expose:
      - build_or_update_graph_tool
      - get_minimal_context_tool
      - get_impact_radius_tool
      - get_review_context_tool
      - query_graph_tool
      - traverse_graph_tool
      - semantic_search_nodes_tool
      - list_graph_stats_tool
      - find_large_functions_tool
      - list_flows_tool
      - get_flow_tool
      - get_affected_flows_tool
      - get_architecture_overview_tool
      - detect_changes_tool
      - get_hub_nodes_tool

capabilities:
  # This repository's own coordinates, written out rather than read from the environment:
  # they are public, they never change, and a literal cannot be unset in a runner.
  #
  # THE ARGUMENT NAMES ARE THE SERVER'S, INCLUDING ITS INCONSISTENCY. The pull-request
  # tools take `pullNumber` (camelCase); the issue tools take `issue_number` (snake_case).
  # `yama doctor` verifies TOOL names against what the server advertises; argument names it
  # cannot check — a server only reports those when a call is made. If a capability fails
  # at run time with "missing required parameter", the name it asks for goes here.

  # --- review phase: available to the main agent from WarmUp onwards, never to a worker.
  #
  # GitHub's server consolidated many read operations behind one tool chosen by a `method`
  # argument. That argument is part of the MAPPING, so it lives here beside the tool name —
  # the code still only ever asks for a capability.
  pr.read:
    tool: github.pull_request_read
    args:
      method: get
      owner: juspay
      repo: yama
      pullNumber: "${pr}"
  comment.list:
    tool: github.pull_request_read
    args:
      method: get_review_comments
      owner: juspay
      repo: yama
      pullNumber: "${pr}"
      # The server pages at 30 threads by default, OLDEST first — a busy pull request's
      # newest comments (the ones dedupe most needs) fall off page one without this.
      perPage: 100

  # --- delivery phase: exposed during Delivery and nowhere else. A review turn reading an
  # attacker-controlled diff must not be holding a tool that can write to the pull request.
  #
  # On this server an inline comment is written into a PENDING review, which has to be
  # created first and submitted after for anyone to see it — that is what the
  # review.begin / review.submit pair below maps. The pair is both-or-neither: each
  # requires the other, and the probe refuses half of it.
  review.begin:
    tool: github.pull_request_review_write
    args:
      method: create
      owner: juspay
      repo: yama
      pullNumber: "${pr}"
  review.submit:
    tool: github.pull_request_review_write
    args:
      method: submit_pending
      event: COMMENT
      owner: juspay
      repo: yama
      pullNumber: "${pr}"
  comment.inline.create:
    tool: github.add_comment_to_pending_review
    args:
      owner: juspay
      repo: yama
      pullNumber: "${pr}"
  comment.summary.create:
    tool: github.add_issue_comment
    args:
      owner: juspay
      repo: yama
      issue_number: "${pr}"

  # Answering a comment that is already on the pull request — the recurring-run case: a
  # finding still open on a second look, under a comment somebody answered or ignored.
  # `commentId` and `body` are the agent's to supply (they vary per call, so they cannot
  # live in a static map); this server wants the NUMERIC id from a #discussion_r anchor,
  # which is exactly what the comment reader takes out of `html_url`.
  comment.reply:
    tool: github.add_reply_to_pull_request_comment
    args:
      owner: juspay
      repo: yama
      pullNumber: "${pr}"

  # The verdict lands as GitHub's own review state: the agent supplies the `event`
  # this platform spells the decision with (BLOCK → REQUEST_CHANGES, COMMENT → COMMENT,
  # APPROVE → APPROVE) — an argument that varies by verdict cannot live in this static
  # map. The delivery gate confirms the tool ran clean, not the agent's account of it.
  verdict.set:
    tool: github.pull_request_review_write
    args:
      method: create_and_submit
      owner: juspay
      repo: yama
      pullNumber: "${pr}"

  # Still off, and deliberately: this repository's descriptions are written by the
  # single-commit policy's own template. Map it when that changes.
  # pr.describe:
  #   tool: github.update_pull_request
  #   args: { owner: juspay, repo: yama, pullNumber: "${pr}" }

# .yama/mcp.yaml — MCP servers, and the capability map (GitHub).
#
# THE CAPABILITY MAP IS THE WHOLE POINT. Yama's code never spells a platform tool name:
# it asks for a CAPABILITY, and this file says which tool provides it. Moving to another
# forge is an edit here, not a code change.
#
# Two forms are accepted:
#
#   <capability>: <server>.<tool>                       # the tool, nothing else
#
#   <capability>:                                       # the tool plus the arguments
#     tool: <server>.<tool>                             # every call of it needs
#     args: { owner: "${GITHUB_OWNER}", pull_number: "${pr}" }
#
# In `args`, `${pr}` / `${branch}` / `${base}` / `${mode}` come from the run target and
# everything else is an environment variable, expanded at load time and loud when unset.
#
# An unmapped capability is switched OFF, never broken.
#
# TOOL NAMES AND ARGUMENT NAMES DIFFER BETWEEN MCP SERVER VERSIONS. Run `yama doctor` after
# `yama init`: it connects each server, prints exactly which tools it exposes, and marks any
# capability pointing at a name that is not there as BROKEN. Fix those rows here and re-run
# it. Argument names it cannot check for you — the server reports those only when a call is
# made — so if a capability fails at run time with "missing required parameter", the name it
# asks for goes here. The names below are `@modelcontextprotocol/server-github`'s: snake_case
# (`pull_number`, `issue_number`), not camelCase.
#
# Note what is NOT here: nothing maps the diff. Yama takes it from git
# (merge-base(base, head)..head), which is deterministic, costs no API call, and reads the
# same on every forge — the platform is only ever asked for comments and the verdict.

version: 1

servers:
  github:
    transport: stdio
    command: npx
    args: ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"]
    env:
      GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN: "${GITHUB_TOKEN}"
    # Fail fast: heavyweight platform reads can exceed the default request window on a
    # large pull request, and each hung call costs a minute of review wall-clock. Code
    # is read locally from the checkout; platform calls are metadata-sized.
    timeoutMs: 30000

capabilities:
  # --- review phase: readable by the main agent at any stage, never by a worker
  pr.read:
    tool: github.get_pull_request
    args:
      owner: "${GITHUB_OWNER}"
      repo: "${GITHUB_REPO}"
      pull_number: "${pr}"
  # pr.diff is deliberately unmapped — see the note above. Map it only if you want the
  # agent to be able to ask the platform for the diff as well as reading it from git.
  comment.list:
    tool: github.get_pull_request_comments
    args:
      owner: "${GITHUB_OWNER}"
      repo: "${GITHUB_REPO}"
      pull_number: "${pr}"
      # Ask for the biggest page the server allows: comment listings page at ~30 by
      # default, oldest first, and marker dedup is blind to anything past page one.
      perPage: 100

  # --- delivery phase: exposed to the main agent during Delivery and nowhere else
  comment.inline.create:
    tool: github.create_pull_request_review_comment
    args:
      owner: "${GITHUB_OWNER}"
      repo: "${GITHUB_REPO}"
      pull_number: "${pr}"
  comment.summary.create:
    tool: github.add_issue_comment
    args:
      owner: "${GITHUB_OWNER}"
      repo: "${GITHUB_REPO}"
      issue_number: "${pr}"
  # Answering a comment already on the pull request. What it is for is the recurring run:
  # a finding still open on a second look, under a comment somebody answered or ignored —
  # re-posting it would duplicate, saying nothing leaves a stale reply standing. The agent
  # supplies `commentId` and `body`; this tool wants the numeric id from a #discussion_r
  # anchor, which is what the comment reader already takes out of `html_url`.
  comment.reply:
    tool: github.add_reply_to_pull_request_comment
    args:
      owner: "${GITHUB_OWNER}"
      repo: "${GITHUB_REPO}"
      pullNumber: "${pr}"
  # comment.update:
  #   tool: github.update_pull_request_review_comment
  #   args: { owner: "${GITHUB_OWNER}", repo: "${GITHUB_REPO}" }
  # verdict.set:
  #   tool: github.create_pull_request_review
  #   args: { owner: "${GITHUB_OWNER}", repo: "${GITHUB_REPO}", pull_number: "${pr}" }
  # pr.describe:
  #   tool: github.update_pull_request
  #   args: { owner: "${GITHUB_OWNER}", repo: "${GITHUB_REPO}", pull_number: "${pr}" }

  # On forges where an inline comment is written into a PENDING review (GitHub's
  # consolidated hosted server), map the lifecycle pair — BOTH or NEITHER, the probe
  # refuses half of it. Servers where an inline comment is one call need neither.
  #
  # review.begin:
  #   tool: github.pull_request_review_write
  #   args: { method: create, owner: "${GITHUB_OWNER}", repo: "${GITHUB_REPO}", pullNumber: "${pr}" }
  # review.submit:
  #   tool: github.pull_request_review_write
  #   args: { method: submit_pending, event: COMMENT, owner: "${GITHUB_OWNER}", repo: "${GITHUB_REPO}", pullNumber: "${pr}" }

# --- OPTIONAL: an extra analysis server, exposed to the review stages ------------------
# Any server may carry `expose:` — bare tool names offered to the REVIEW stages of the
# main session (never delivery, never posting). Each name is proved against what the
# server advertises at connect time; a missing tool or a failed spawn is a named
# degradation, never a failed review. Example — a tree-sitter code graph:
#
# code-review-graph:
#   transport: stdio
#   command: uvx
#   args: ["--from", "code-review-graph==2.3.7", "code-review-graph", "serve"]
